steps.instruction: Open http://127.0.0.1:3000/ in the browser. If the Grafana login page appears, sign in with username 'admin' and password 'admin'; if Grafana then asks you to change the admin password, click 'Skip'. Then find and open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use the Dashboards search in the left menu). Report the exact titles of all panels shown on that dashboard, exactly as they are displayed on screen.

recorded.panel_titles: Request rate, Error count, Latency by endpoint

steps.instruction: In Grafana, create a NEW dashboard (New dashboard / Add new dashboard). Add a 'Stat' visualization panel. Set the panel's title to exactly '{{runid}} Availability'. For its query, select the 'TestData' data source (it may be called 'TestData' or 'grafana-testdata-datasource' - pick the TestData one) and use the scenario 'Random Walk' (or whatever default scenario is offered) so the query returns data. Then set the dashboard title to exactly '{{runid}} {{01-open.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' and SAVE the dashboard (click Save, give it that title if prompted, confirm Save). Report the panel title shown, the data source name used, and the dashboard URL from the browser address bar after saving.

In Grafana, open the dashboard titled '{{runid}} {{01-open.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' (it is at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/). Enter edit mode (Dashboard menu -> Edit dashboard). Add a NEW panel of type 'Text' and set its title to exactly '{{runid}} Notes'. Set the text content to include the runid '{{runid}}' (for example: 'Notes for run {{runid}} - bench dashboard created via automation.'). Apply the change, then SAVE the dashboard (click Save, confirm Save, wait for the '{{02-create.save_status}}' toast). Report the exact panel title shown on the dashboard, the text content displayed, and confirm the save succeeded.

steps.instruction: In Grafana, open the dashboard '{{runid}} {{01-open.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/ . Do two things and save: (1) Add the tag 'bench' to the dashboard - use the dashboard settings (gear/cog icon -> Settings -> General, or the dashboard menu -> Dashboard settings) and add the tag 'bench' in the Tags field. (2) Set the dashboard's time range to the last 6 hours using the time picker in the top bar (choose 'Last 6 hours'). Then SAVE the dashboard: click Save, and in the save dialog make sure the checkbox 'Update default time range' IS TICKED (this is required so the 6-hour range is persisted into the saved dashboard), then confirm Save and wait for the '{{02-create.save_status}}' toast. Report the tag(s) shown in dashboard settings, the time range shown in the top bar, and whether the 'Update default time range' checkbox was ticked when you saved.

recorded.save_result: saved (dashboard version 3; save drawer shows no pending changes)

steps.instruction: In Grafana, open the dashboard '{{runid}} {{01-open.dashboard_folder}} Dashboard' at http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{02-create.url.p1}}/ . Set the dashboard's auto-refresh interval to '1m' (one minute). This is done either via the refresh-interval dropdown next to the time picker in the top bar (click the refresh interval selector and choose '1m'), or via dashboard Settings -> General -> Auto refresh. Then SAVE the dashboard (click Save, confirm Save, wait for the save to complete). After saving, verify persistence by opening dashboard Settings -> JSON Model (or reloading the page) and confirm the 'refresh' field is set to '1m'. Report the auto-refresh value shown in the top bar and the 'refresh' value read from the JSON model.
